questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a destination, where there were universities, that offered courses or projects, that could substitute my obligatory courses. I also wanted to go to a destination, that would help me improve my language skills. So I choose Montpellier because I had French in high-school and I wanted to improve so that I would be able to have academic conversations. It was of course also crucial for me that the destination was safe and that it had some good opportunities to enjoy my freetime as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's been an amazing experience! I've learned so much and I've had the best time here. The only reason why I haven't given it 10/10, is because it's been a little messy with my supervisors and with the communication of the courses and what was obligatory to go to and what was expected of me because it is not the same as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was manageable, but there was a lot. You can easily get overwhelmed. But I managed because the people at the International Relations Office are really nice and they will gladly explain things.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from the International Relations and I got help from a friend, who lives here.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I arrived pretty late because I had exams in Copenhagen, while some of the introduction courses were going on, so I didn't receive all the information at first. I struggled a little in the beginning, but there was some introductions and a French students took a group of us (Erasmus students) on a tour of campus and explained some things to us and gave us his contact information, so we could always ask.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through CROUS, which is a company that has a lot of different student residence buildings. You can go to their website and request a room and then they'll tell you what's available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very convenient to get a bike to go to campus. You can get around very easily - there are actually bikelanes on most roads! If you don't get a bike, there are also a lot of public transportation options (there are multiple tram lines and busses).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult because I basically did it through a lot of emails back and fourth with one of the professors in Montpellier.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Relations and the professor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. It all worked out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Begin early and keep sending them emails if they don't reply. They might not have seen your email.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one bachelor course, but it was in French, so the level was pretty fitting for me. I did two projects, which were both challenging academically and then I had a course in English, that was very different from what I was used to, so it also challenged me in that sense.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty similar other than the fact that the students talk during the lectures. If they think it's boring, they will just start small-talking and the professor doesn't really care.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Entrepreneurship
Nutrition Humaine
Project: INFOGEST digestion
Project: Consumer Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It's difficult to say because the projects were a really big part of my semester, but the Nutrition course was good. The Entrepreneurship course was a little messy, so maybe try to find something different if you need that kind of course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It costs money to go to the doctor and I was surprised how expensive it is. It also costs a lot of money to get bloodtests etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It's a little cheaper to buy food in the supermarket than in Denmark, but when you go out for dinner, the prices are pretty much the same as in Copenhagen (maybe a little cheaper).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities available. I didn't attend any of the ones at the university though because I was too late to get the approval from the doctor and then I couldn't sign up. I did sign up to a gym though and that was a really good quality gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be a part of the Erasmus Life Montpellier group and the ESN Montpellier. They have so many events, where you meet all the other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Pic Saint-Loup, go to the beaches Carnon and La Grande-Motte. Travel around - go to Nîmes, Marseille, Lyon and all the other charming French cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as soon as I got more comfortable with speaking French and as soon as I made some friends and got settled into my residence.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take initiative and be open and don't be afraid to speak French.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the French are pretty laissez-faire. They are not very punctual and it can be difficult to make appointments with them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are very kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare to feel overwhelmed in the beginning, but don't worry - you'll feel at home within a couple of weeks. 
Practice your French. A lot of people don't speak English very well.
Ask for help - they will happily help you out!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it's important to be ready to be very social and open.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I made and all the experiences we had together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get comfortable with the French systems and the French way to do things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
